title: Stroke (FAST)
summary: Use FAST to recognise a stroke. Call immediately and record the time symptoms started – treatment depends on it.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} immediately – time is critical
when: Any one of the FAST signs, even if it goes away
Sudden confusion, loss of balance, loss of vision or severe headache with no known cause

steps.title: F – Face
steps.text: Ask them to smile. Does one side of the face droop?

steps.title: A – Arms
steps.text: Ask them to raise both arms. Does one arm drift down or can they not lift it?

steps.title: S – Speech
steps.text: Ask them to repeat a simple phrase. Is their speech slurred or strange, or can they not speak?

steps.title: T – Time to call {EMERGENCY}
steps.text: If you see any of these signs, call immediately. Note the time symptoms started or when they were last seen well.

steps.title: While you wait
steps.text: Keep them comfortable and reassured. If they become unresponsive and are breathing, place them in the recovery position. Be ready to start CPR.

doNot: Do not give food, drink or medicines (including aspirin) – swallowing may be affected
Do not let them drive or wait to 'see if it passes'

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)
